notes: Every asserted element matches what I recorded: one standing poler behind two seated hooded passengers, long pole, upright blades clustered between the passengers and the bow, battlemented stone tower on the left bank, low ridge on the far shore, bundle/sack on the boat floor, belt pouch, rust-red cloak, engraved cross-hatching and ruled border with corner flourishes. The text deliberately avoids stating a sword count and self-flags it as uncertain, which matches my own null count.

issues.existing: hanging lantern with warm glow at the boat's stern
issues.observed: the lit lantern hangs from an ornate finial post at the right-hand end of the boat — the same end the text itself calls the bow, outboard of and beyond the row of upright swords
issues.evidence: In the image the standing poling figure is at the left end, the seated figure is mid-hull, the swords stand to their right, and the glowing lantern hangs furthest right of all, past the swords, on a decorated post over the water. The text's own spatialRelations place the bow toward the right and the swords in the bow, so putting the lantern at the stern contradicts the pixels and is internally inconsistent.

issues.existing: exact number of swords standing in the bow (appears to be six, some overlapping)
issues.observed: I can individually resolve five hilts/blades; a sixth is not establishable — the pale palette and overlapping shafts prevent a reliable count in either direction
issues.evidence: Five distinct pommel/cross-guard clusters are separable left-to-right above the gunwale; whatever lies to the right of them cannot be separated from the lantern post's shaft. This is flagged as unverifiable, not as a different number.

notes: Matches my record: two dark near-silhouetted figures standing face to face, a small lit stemmed cup with a pale flower between them at centre, a horizontal row of five rectangular wall recesses each holding one stemmed goblet, a staircase rising at the right, cracked stone floor, frayed trailing robe hems.
